domain: Japanese woodblock prints — Edo period and Utagawa school
contextNote: Ukiyo-e were produced as commercial multiples. Artist attribution is therefore not about uniqueness but about identifying the correct design, publisher, and impression period. The key distinction is not WHETHER a print is by a named artist but WHICH impression and period it represents — value differentials between early Edo and later Meiji reprints can be 5-15x. All prints carry woodblock-printed artist signatures and publisher seals rather than hand signatures — absence of hand signature is normal.

criticalAuthenticationMarkers.authenticIndicator: Smooth, subtle gradation — no banding or hard edges
criticalAuthenticationMarkers.reprintIndicator: Banded or mechanical-looking gradation; simplified or absent

criticalAuthenticationMarkers.authenticIndicator: Natural 0.5–2mm misregistration consistent with hand printing
criticalAuthenticationMarkers.reprintIndicator: Perfect mechanical registration (photomechanical) or excessive misregistration (worn blocks)

criticalAuthenticationMarkers.authenticIndicator: Rich, saturated colour with clear differentiation
criticalAuthenticationMarkers.reprintIndicator: Washed-out colour; bleed between areas; loss of fine line detail

criticalAuthenticationMarkers.authenticIndicator: Irregular fibrous texture; slight thickness variation; warm cream/ivory tone
criticalAuthenticationMarkers.reprintIndicator: Uniform machine-smooth texture; bright white tone

criticalAuthenticationMarkers.authenticIndicator: Appropriate seal type for claimed period; clearly printed
criticalAuthenticationMarkers.reprintIndicator: Absent where expected; blurred; wrong type for claimed period

distinguishingFeatures: Machine-made paper more common in later Meiji
